answer.label: Spoken by
answer.authorDates: 1955–2011 · co-founder & CEO of Apple; CEO of Pixar · said 12 June 2005
answer.sourceLine: This is a real sentence from Jobs’s 2005 Stanford University Commencement Address, delivered 12 June 2005. It appears verbatim in Stanford’s own published text and in the video of the speech: “…the only way to do great work is to love what you do.”

source.heading: The source

docMeta.dd: Steve Jobs, CEO of Apple & Pixar

source.excerpt: You’ve got to find what you love. And that is as true for your work as it is for your lovers. Your work is going to fill a large part of your life, and the only way to be truly satisfied is to do what you believe is great work. And the only way to do great work is to love what you do. If you haven’t found it yet, keep looking. Don’t settle.
trail: Stanford published the full prepared text and video of the 12 June 2005 address on its own site: news.stanford.edu ↗.
Independent transcripts reproduce the line verbatim — e.g. jamesclear.com ↗ and rev.com ↗.
The underlying “do what you love” idea is older and is often mis-credited to Confucius — Quote Investigator ↗ traces that separate saying only to the 1980s.
source.cutTag: ↑ the popular one-liner is lifted from the middle of this passage
source.excerptNote: The sentence is almost always quoted on its own, but in the speech it is the hinge of a longer thought: satisfaction comes from great work, and great work comes from love of the work — hence “keep looking, don’t settle.”

author.name: Steve Jobs
author.heading: About Steve Jobs
author.bio: Steven Paul Jobs (1955–2011) co-founded Apple in 1976, was forced out in 1985, and returned in 1997 to lead its revival with the iMac, iPod, iPhone and iPad. He was also CEO of Pixar. His 2005 Stanford Commencement Address — built around three personal stories and the closing charge to “Stay Hungry. Stay Foolish.” — became one of the most-watched speeches ever recorded.

misattribution.heading: The idea is older than Jobs — and often mis-credited
misattribution.intro: The specific sentence is genuinely Steve Jobs’s. The confusion is about the underlying idea — “do work you love” — which long predates 2005 and is regularly pinned on people who never said it.

items.scope: The related maxim wrongly attributed to
items.why: “Choose a job you love, and you will never have to work a day in your life” is constantly credited to Confucius, but Quote Investigator ↗ finds no basis for it and traces the saying only to the 1980s. It is a different line from Jobs’s, but the two are frequently blurred together.
Gibran’s The Prophet (1923) — “Work is love made visible” — expresses a similar spirit and is occasionally cited as if it were the source of Jobs’s wording. It is a thematic ancestor, not the quote.

misattribution.truthLine: Bottom line: the exact sentence is Steve Jobs’s own, from his 2005 Stanford Commencement Address ↗ — but the broader “love your work” idea is much older and is not original to him.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Jobs delivered the address a year after his first cancer surgery, and its second story culminates in this line. Framed by his own firing from Apple and his return, the sentence lands not as breezy advice but as hard-won: love of the work is what carried him through being “an overnight failure.”
The speech has since become the most-watched commencement address on record, and this sentence is its most-quoted fragment — printed on posters, graduation cards, and startup walls worldwide.
context.detailsSummary: The counter-argument that grew up around it
detailsBody: The advice has drawn a notable backlash. Critics — including a widely shared 2024 Fortune essay ↗ and Cal Newport’s So Good They Can’t Ignore You — argue that “follow your passion” is survivorship-biased and can mislead people who don’t yet have a passion to follow.

Ironically, Jobs himself often framed his own path less as pre-existing passion than as persistence: he stayed with the work because he loved doing it, not because he had identified a calling in advance.
context.pull: The only way to be truly satisfied is to do what you believe is great work. And the only way to do great work is to love what you do.
